description: Four independently chosen prefixes: PUT17 then SCAN[10,20], reverse order, same-base PUT10 then SCAN[10,20] control, and outside-range PUT21 control. Actual owner emissions reach a third acceptor; compare its reply dependency against the actual state conflict predicate for the sole prior.

harness.description: Bounded synchronous replicas with production handlers and serialized PreAccept messages/replies.
semantic_changes: Bound instance allocation and omit autonomous transport/execution/timers.
Capture actual SendMsg bytes in buffers; deliver selected valid first-instance messages once in source order.
Emit input conflict classification and response dependency with no protocol edits.

legality.derivation: For each input case, fresh constructor-equivalent N=5,F=2 state is allocated. Owner0 emits its first valid command to preferred peers1/2, and the actual bytes for peer2 are decoded and dispatched. Owner1 then emits its first valid command to peers2/3. Before delivery the harness checks the sole known prior is uncommitted, all next.Deps are -1 and no other instance exists at the acceptor. Earlier row0 differs from incoming row1, and acceptor2 differs from both, so row exemptions cannot hide the tested relation. SCAN operands use the same little-endian count encoding as SendScan. state.ConflictBatch is evaluated on the actual prior and incoming decoded commands before input admission. handlePreAccept then runs and the real fresh reply is decoded. Ballot, fresh status and vector size are checked; actual Deps[prior.Replica]>=prior.Instance supplies covers_prior. All observations are single-owner synchronous reads. Remaining outbound messages are never asserted complete or used as consensus support.
legality.applicability: No faults, reordering, recovery or background executor; four cases fixed before observations.

grounding.derivation: The independently evaluated input.conflicts is the antecedent; it is not a result-based applicability filter. Only when the state layer reports a conflict must covers_prior hold. Identity scenario/replica/instance matches the later reply without comparing a dependency value as identity. The out-of-range case may satisfy the implication vacuously and does not establish completeness of the index.
grounding.applicability: One known prior and one fresh response per declared scenario.

observable_properties.description: An actual state-level conflict implies returned coverage of the only known predecessor.

uncertainties: No endpoint consistency model or whole-cluster consequence is established by this local comparison.
